messages:
maria.s: Hey team — ACME support ticket says their March 15 invoice has ~2x token usage vs dashboard. They claim no traffic spike. Can someone look?
ian.support: copying logs now, have the customer correlation id?
maria.s: ticket includes request-id `req_8a3f9` and customer session id `sess-ACME-77`.
dee.sre: I pulled gateway logs for req_8a3f9 — I see two upstream deliveries 2025-03-15T14:02:10Z and 2025-03-15T14:02:12Z. Gateway retried after a 401 from auth service.
ingress-bot: [automated] proxy-retry: req_8a3f9 upstream_attempts=2 reason=auth_refresh status_before_retry=401
ian.support: can you paste the two entries?
dee.sre: sure — snippet: ```
2025-03-15T14:02:10.123Z gateway id=req_8a3f9 upstream_status=502 auth_token=expired attempt=1
2025-03-15T14:02:12.456Z gateway id=req_8a3f9 upstream_status=200 auth_token=refreshed attempt=2
```
maria.s: customer SDK says they sent a single request. They use short-lived ephemeral tokens that rotate halfway through the request window.
beth.billing: If upstream got two successful deliveries to the model serving plane we would meter both. Need to confirm what the serving runtime saw.
dee.sre: checked runtime logs — model-infer shows two separate call_ids: `call-77-a` and `call-77-b`, both with ~1.2k tokens. Body content identical. No idempotency-key header present in either.
ian.support: that explains doubled token count. Why wasn't the gateway deduping? I thought we dedupe on idempotency-key + body hash.
dee.sre: dedupe only runs when client provides an Idempotency-Key header. This customer relies on ephemeral auth and assumed retries are transparent. When auth refresh triggers a proxy replay we currently replay the entire request without injecting an idempotency key.
maria.s: customer is asking for refund and a mitigation timeline. They attached their request trace showing only one send.
beth.billing: will coordinate refund once engineering confirms. Estimate impact: ~3k tokens * 2 = ~3.6k extra tokens — small but customer upset.
ian.support: repro steps I used locally: 
1) Start nginx auth proxy that returns 401 for first token, then 200 after refresh.
2) Client sends request without Idempotency-Key header.
3) Gateway retries the request after auth refresh.
Command: ```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ephemeral-v1" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Result: gateway forwarded twice.
dee.sre: logs from gateway show we call the auth service and then immediately replay the buffered request on token renewal. We should either: (a) add automatic idempotency-key generation for retries, or (b) only replay if body/headers unchanged and runtime supports dedupe by body-hash.
maria.s: can we quick-patch to avoid more customers being hit? Even a gateway config change would help.
dee.sre: short-term: enable body-hash dedupe for replayed requests at gateway (cheap). Implementation: compute sha256(body) + path + method and check recent cache for duplicate delivered body in 2s window. For safety, only dedupe when Authorization header was the only differing header.
ian.support: is there any risk of false-positives for idempotent endpoints?
dee.sre: risk minimal for generation endpoints with synchronous semantics — but we'll whitelist endpoints where we apply it.
beth.billing: after patch we should scan invoices for last 30 days for similar patterns and proactively refund.
maria.s: customer is ok with refund and wants a fix timeline. Can we get an ETA?
dee.sre: I can ship the gateway cache dedupe patch to canary in ~48 hours, full rollout in 5 days if no regressions.
ian.support: will reply to ACME: refund initiated pending engineering confirmation, and we expect patch in ~2 days.
maria.s: ping beth when refund initiated.
beth.billing: noted — I'll prepare the credit once dee confirms which invoice lines to adjust.
ingress-bot: [automated] incident-link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3345 (gateway: dedupe replayed requests on auth-refresh)
ian.support: follow-up question — should SDKs be updated to always send Idempotency-Key on mutating/generate calls? That would avoid a lot of this.
dee.sre: yes, we'll add SDK guidance in the PR plus conservative server-side dedupe. Dual approach recommended.
maria.s: thanks all — I'll update the customer and close the ticket once refund is posted. :+1:
beth.billing: refund posted 2025-03-16T09:10:00Z — customer acknowledged.
ian.support: closing action items: 1) dee to open PR for gateway dedupe (INF-3345) 2) eng-docs update for SDK idempotency guidance 3) billing to scan/repeat credits for similar invoices 4) notify CS to prioritize customers with ephemeral auth.
maria.s: done, adding notes to the support ticket and tagging the customer success lead. Thanks!
